import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Prepare the data
# We want to visualize the number of dog registrations per year,
# broken down by the dog's gender.
# 'StichtagDatJahr' represents the year of registration.
# 'SexHundLang' represents the dog's gender (männlich=male, weiblich=female).

# Group by year and dog gender, then count the occurrences
# The .size() method counts the number of rows in each group.
# .unstack() pivots the 'SexHundLang' column to create separate columns for each gender,
# making it suitable for a stacked bar chart.
df_plot = df.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'SexHundLang']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Rename columns to English for clarity in the legend
# Assuming 'männlich' maps to 'Male' and 'weiblich' maps to 'Female'.
df_plot = df_plot.rename(columns={'männlich': 'Male', 'weiblich': 'Female'})

# Set the style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the stacked bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Plotting the data as a stacked bar chart
df_plot.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=plt.gca(), cmap='viridis')

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Annual Dog Registrations in Zurich by Dog Gender', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Year of Registration', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if years are numerous
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Add a legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with bars
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='12',
           bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Improve layout and add a grid for better readability
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.9, 1]) # Adjust layout to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
